units.title: The data-to-evaluation lifecycle and ownership of every state
outcomes: Map your existing corpus, decoder, pretraining, adaptation, preference, RL, multimodal and safety artifacts into one experiment graph.
Name the writer, immutable identity, consumers and recovery rule for each state.
Explain why the training reward and the independent evaluator need separate ownership.
units.why: Earlier units proved individual components. Integration asks whether a reported result can be traced through the same data, policy and evaluator identities without an undocumented handoff.

next.note: Attach the lifecycle graph to actual code paths and artifacts.

study.title: LLM Post-Training Laboratory: state contracts
study.locator: Core requirements, Architecture constraints, Deliverables and Milestones A to C
study.depth: Audit the artifacts already built in lmlab. Do not restart the full laboratory or add another training stage.

study.title: OLMo 2: infrastructure and evaluation handoffs
study.locator: arXiv:2501.00656v3, Sections 6.1 to 6.3; Appendix A.1 and A.2, including Tables 20 and 21
study.depth: Read the cluster descriptions for storage, isolation and ownership boundaries, not as a deployment assignment. Compare evaluation contracts, not the paper's scores with your small model.

focus: Use one root manifest to connect raw-document lineage, tokenizer and templates, model configuration, optimizer and sampler state, checkpoints, adapters, reference policy, reward or verifier, rollouts and evaluation outputs.

A role can share a process with another role and still own different state. The learner updates the policy; rollout generation consumes a particular policy version; scoring consumes a particular reward or verifier version.
Carry the image-text module and the safety release record as versioned branches of the same graph. A missing component is an explicit evidence gap, not an implied successful stage.
Reuse Complete checkpoints, atomic writes and reproducibility boundaries. Here the new question is which downstream artifacts become stale when an upstream identity changes.
units.reproduce: Without notes, draw the path from one corpus document to a training batch, checkpoint, post-training policy, generated answer and independent score. Add the reference and reward branches, then mark the owner and identity on every edge. Replace the tokenizer identity on paper and list the descendants that must be rebuilt or revalidated.
traps: Calling a directory name an immutable version. Reusing the name can silently attach old evaluation to new weights.
Treating a reference policy, rollout policy and current learner policy as interchangeable because their architecture is identical.
Calling a connected dashboard a connected lifecycle. The join must reach the actual inputs, outputs and state identities.

selfTest.q: Why is a checkpoint step number insufficient to identify an evaluation target?
selfTest.a: Different runs can use the same step. Bind the score to a run identity and checkpoint content digest, plus tokenizer, template and generation configuration.

selfTest.q: Can the reward model also be the only external evaluator?
selfTest.a: No. Optimizing its score can exploit its errors. Use independent task and safety evidence, with their own versions and calibration records.

selfTest.q: Does sharing weights imply sharing optimizer state?
selfTest.a: No. An inference export can preserve model behavior while omitting optimizer, sampler and RNG state needed to continue training.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's root lifecycle manifest, state-ownership table and descendant-invalidation audit.
units.stopWhen: An answer and score can be traced to their corpus, checkpoint and post-training ancestors, and every state has one declared writer and a recovery rule.

fit.note: The laboratory supplies the lifecycle and state contract; OLMo 2 supplies real infrastructure and evaluator handoffs. The mini-project joins the existing artifacts.

units.title: Experiment lineage and reconstructing a real training codebase
outcomes: Trace one real SFT path from launch arguments through tokenization, masking, loss, update and checkpoint publication.
Attach resolved configuration, source revision, environment and artifact digests to each experiment edge.
Separate a historical released recipe from the current code path used for your modification.
units.why: A recipe name does not specify an experiment. Reconstructing the executed path exposes configuration overrides and hidden transformations before they become explanations for a gain.

next.note: Budget the resolved workload rather than a recipe's defaults.

study.title: Open Instruct: reconstruct the SFT execution path
study.locator: `FlatArguments`, `main`, dataset construction with `get_cached_dataset_tulu`, model and optimizer construction, training loop, checkpoint and final-save branches
study.depth: Read, do not launch the default recipe. Follow `sft_tokenize_mask_out_prompt_v1` and `mask_labels` in `dataset_transformation.py` at the same revision. Keep native evaluation launchers outside your independent evaluation path.

study.title: The Turing Way: capture the execution environment
study.locator: Reproducible Environments: Summary, What is a Computational Environment?, and Motivation and Background (page read 2026-10-16)

focus: Record the effective values after CLI overrides, model loading and dataset transformations. A configuration file alone omits runtime decisions and inherited defaults.

Trace a real message into token IDs and labels, then into the scalar loss and optimizer update. Distinguish final-assistant-only targets from all-assistant targets; the two named masking paths have different contracts.

Use the earlier Dependency locks, run manifests and quality gates result. Add dataset-transform fingerprints, upstream checkpoint digests and evaluator identity rather than another generic environment tutorial.

Read the OLMo 2 release as a historical case. A newer OLMo-core or Open Instruct revision does not retroactively identify the code that trained that release. Record unknown historical edges as unknown.
units.reproduce: Close the source and reconstruct the SFT call graph from arguments to saved policy. Reopen it and correct each unsupported edge. In lmlab, serialize one resolved run record and verify every parent digest before accepting its outputs; changing a parent identity must invalidate that binding rather than relabel an old result.
traps: Recording a Git commit while ignoring an uncommitted patch. Store both the base revision and the patch digest.
Treating a dataset cache hit as proof that tokenizer, template and filtering settings match. Check the cache's identity contract.
Tracing only the forward call. Reduction, accumulation, clipping and scheduler placement can change the effective objective or update.

selfTest.q: What does a clean source revision fail to identify?
selfTest.a: Data and model revisions, resolved arguments, environment, external evaluators and any local patch. Those belong in the run record too.

selfTest.q: Why inspect both prompt masking and the training loss?
selfTest.a: Correct labels can still receive wrong weighting through reduction or accumulation. Trace which tokens contribute and their denominator through the update.

selfTest.q: An old checkpoint loads under current code. Have you reconstructed its training recipe?
selfTest.a: No. Load compatibility establishes only that loading succeeded. Historical code, configuration, data and update semantics still need evidence.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's annotated real-code trace, resolved run record and parent-identity rejection tests.
units.stopWhen: Your trace names the executed data, masking, objective, update and save functions, and a changed upstream identity is caught before old outputs enter a comparison.

fit.note: The pinned SFT source reaches implementation depth and the environment guide supports packaging. The mini-project turns the trace into executable lineage checks.

units.title: Compute, memory and checkpoint budgets with uncertainty, and the parallelism interface
outcomes: Derive separate training, rollout, evaluation, host-memory and checkpoint budgets for one experiment.
Specify what data, tensor, pipeline, sequence and expert parallelism would partition and communicate.
Defend a feasible plan using ranges for unknown workspace, bandwidth and failure overhead.
units.why: The useful budget is the cost of answering a research question, including baselines, failed attempts and evaluation. A model that fits alone may not fit beside a reference policy or rollout buffers.

next.note: Freeze these predictions before measuring the local run.

study.title: How to Scale Your Model: training ownership and communication
study.locator: Part 5: What Do We Mean By Scaling?, Data Parallelism, Fully-Sharded Data Parallelism, Tensor Parallelism, Combining FSDP and Tensor Parallelism, and Pipelining (page read 2026-10-16)
study.depth: Use the diagrams and forward/backward algorithms for an analytical plan only. The two-matrix MLP omits attention and gating. The 10-byte parameter ledger excludes gradients and other live storage; add them. Overlap is an assumption, not a guaranteed saving.

study.title: Sequence and expert interfaces on GPU systems
study.locator: Part 12: Expert Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism and Caveat about latency; Part 5's Note [context parallelism] (pages read 2026-10-16)
study.depth: Identify dispatch, combine and sequence exchange boundaries. Do not adopt the source hardware constants or implement a distributed runtime.

study.title: Budget the whole study
study.locator: Q8, Experiments Compute Resource, including preliminary and failed experiments (page read 2026-10-16)

focus: Build on Counting parameters and FLOPs and Memory, arithmetic intensity and reconciling estimates. List every live tensor by owner, shape and dtype; separate device peak, host staging and durable storage.

DP partitions examples and combines gradients; TP partitions tensor work; PP partitions layers. Sequence or context partitioning needs attention exchanges. EP moves routed tokens to expert owners and back. State which axes are independent and which reuse ranks.
Count valid training tokens separately from padded input tokens, generated tokens and verifier calls. More TP, PP or sequence ranks do not create more unique examples.

Give both a single-device plan and an analytical distributed alternative. Include checkpoint copies, conversion scratch space, reference and reward models, and uncertainty intervals that could reverse the preferred plan.
units.reproduce: For a synthetic 12-million-parameter model with BF16 weights and gradients, two FP32 Adam moments and no master weights, derive 144,000,000 bytes of persistent training tensors. A weights-plus-moments checkpoint contains 120,000,000 tensor bytes before metadata; it omits gradients. Add activation, workspace, host staging and storage reserves separately. For microbatch 2 sequences, accumulation 4 and length 128 on one data replica, derive 1,024 input tokens per update, then budget all experiment arms and evaluation.
traps: Treating the synthetic dtype ledger as a PyTorch optimizer default. Inspect the tensors your chosen implementation actually stores.
Dividing every memory term by every parallelism degree. Gather buffers and replicated tensors do not obey that shortcut.
Using peak FLOP/s or link bandwidth as attained throughput. State the assumed rates and test sensitivity to them.

selfTest.q: Does a 120,000,000-byte weights-plus-moments checkpoint imply that the synthetic model trains in that much memory?
selfTest.a: No. Even the stated persistent training tensors need 144,000,000 bytes. Activations, workspace and runtime storage are additional.

selfTest.q: Can a sequence split be treated as ordinary DP for attention?
selfTest.a: Not generally. Queries can depend on keys and values held by other sequence owners, so attention needs an explicit exchange and masking contract.

selfTest.q: What if the estimated best plan loses at the low end of the bandwidth range?
selfTest.a: The ranking is unresolved under that uncertainty. Measure the decisive rate or choose a more robust feasible alternative; do not report a guaranteed winner.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's whole-study resource ledger, single-device feasibility check and analytical parallelism alternative with sensitivity ranges.
units.stopWhen: Every arm fits a declared local budget, every distributed tensor has an owner and transfer boundary, and at least one uncertain assumption has a decision-changing sensitivity check.

fit.note: The scaling-book algorithms cover the analytical interfaces, with explicit limits on their simplified ledger. Q8 and the mini-project extend the budget to the whole study.

units.title: Checkpoint conversion and resharding contracts, and rollout, reward and evaluation service boundaries
outcomes: Distinguish behavior-preserving export, training resume and layout-only resharding contracts.
Specify rollout, reward, verifier and evaluation request identities and rejection rules.
Explain which state cannot be assumed equivalent after a topology or precision change.
units.why: Successful deserialization proves little about the experiment. The consumer must receive the intended model semantics and the state its particular job requires.

next.note: Make broken handoffs diagnosable through joined records.

study.title: OLMo-core: model export is a consumer contract
study.locator: Module description, `parse_args` and `main`: configuration, tokenizer revision, dtype and validation handoff
study.depth: Read only. Do not convert a released large model. Transfer the contract to your existing small checkpoint with fixed token-ID probes and tokenizer round trips.

study.title: OLMo-core: separate resharded tensors from trainer state
study.locator: `config_dicts_from_path` and `_worker_process`: model and optimizer reconstruction, load, copied ancillary files and save
study.depth: Keep resharding analytical. Cross-check `Trainer.load_state_dict` in `src/olmo_core/train/trainer.py` at the same revision: rank RNG restoration is conditional on unchanged world size. Copied trainer files do not prove equivalent continuation.

study.title: Laboratory: immutable service inputs and outputs
study.locator: Architecture constraints and Milestone C, bounded versioned rollout/verification queue and independent behavior evaluation

focus: An export needs parameter-name, shape, dtype, tied-weight, positional and tokenizer semantics. Test fixed-input logits within a justified tolerance, not identical sampled text alone.
A training resume additionally needs optimizer, schedule, data position and RNG. Resharding changes physical ownership; it does not automatically define equivalent random streams or sample order.

A rollout request binds prompt, policy checkpoint, template, decoding configuration and sample identity. Its result preserves generated tokens and behavior-policy log probabilities where the objective needs them.

Reward and evaluation records bind their own scorer version and the immutable response they scored. Stale-policy acceptance, timeouts and invalid responses need explicit policies even when all roles are local function calls.
units.reproduce: Without notes, write three acceptance tables for the same small checkpoint: inference export, same-environment resume and an analytical changed-mesh restore. For each state, mark preserve, remap, regenerate or reject. Add a rollout-to-verifier-to-evaluator record and show exactly which check rejects a response paired with the wrong policy or scorer identity.
traps: Promoting a weights-only export to a resume checkpoint. A compatible forward pass does not reconstruct optimizer history.
Expecting bitwise logits after a dtype change. Quantization and floating-point reduction order can change outputs; choose the comparison and tolerance before conversion.
Recomputing old rollout log probabilities under the current policy and calling them behavior-policy probabilities. That changes the objective's data.

selfTest.q: Why compare token IDs as well as decoded strings after export?
selfTest.a: Different token sequences can decode to similar text while assigning different probabilities and boundaries. Tokenizer and special-token semantics are part of the model interface.

selfTest.q: Do matching full weights after resharding establish exact training continuation?
selfTest.a: No. Optimizer alignment, data ownership, RNG streams and numerical execution also matter. State what was preserved and what was reset.

selfTest.q: May rollout, reward and evaluation services run sequentially on one CPU?
selfTest.a: Yes. These are ownership and record contracts, not a requirement for separate machines. Such a run provides local evidence, not distributed throughput evidence.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's checkpoint-consumer acceptance tests, local rollout/scoring contracts and analytical resharding state table.
units.stopWhen: The three consumer contracts distinguish preserved from missing state, and mismatched policy, tokenizer or scorer identities are refused at the appropriate boundary.

fit.note: Pinned conversion, resharding and trainer source expose actual state boundaries; the laboratory supplies local service contracts. No distributed execution is needed for this explain target.

units.title: Lifecycle observability and failures that span data, checkpoints, policies and evaluators
outcomes: Join data, update, checkpoint, rollout and evaluator events into one causal investigation.
Measure instrumentation overhead separately from the uninstrumented workload.
Localize a seeded cross-component failure and preserve the first bad handoff.
units.why: A rising reward and falling task score can be an objective failure, stale policy, data change or evaluator drift. Joined identities make those explanations distinguishable.

next.note: Turn diagnosis into bounded retry, retention and rollback decisions.

study.title: Laboratory: joined instrumentation and failure campaign
study.locator: Milestone B, Milestone D, Failure-injection requirements and Measurement requirements
study.depth: Select one failure crossing two existing components. Do not repeat all objective probes from earlier sections. Use synthetic or already-approved data.

study.title: OLMo-core: inspect the data-resume identity check
study.locator: `NumpyDataLoaderBase.state_dict` and `load_state_dict`: fingerprint version, fingerprint, counters, seed and epoch
study.depth: Compare the code with your manifest checks. This loader warns on fingerprint-version changes and can explicitly ignore a same-version fingerprint mismatch; do not treat it as unconditional fail-closed validation.

study.title: Fault Tolerance: detect missing progress
study.locator: Is-job-hanging watchdog and Low disk space alerts
study.depth: Use progress and storage signals as vocabulary. No scheduler, notification service or cluster watchdog installation is required.

focus: Extend Metrics, logs, traces, correlation and cardinality with run, artifact, batch, policy and evaluator joins. Put unbounded item IDs in event records, not metric labels.
Keep valid-token denominators, data-source exposure, loss, gradient and update norms, phase times and memory alongside rollout lag, length, reward, invalid counts and external outcomes.

Choose competing hypotheses before inspecting the answer. A wrong dataset version after resume should be visible in the checkpoint-to-loader join; evaluator drift should be visible when rescoring unchanged outputs.
Use the first bad boundary, an independent oracle and a targeted rerun to establish the root cause. Correlated metric changes alone do not establish causation.
units.reproduce: Replay saved responses from one lmlab policy with the original scorer, then deliberately attach a changed parser or verifier identity. Trace the discrepancy through response digest, scorer version and item denominator without retraining. Separately replay a synthetic checkpoint manifest against a changed dataset digest and require refusal before the next batch. Keep the original evidence and the seeded incident in separate attempt records.
traps: Averaging failed and successful attempts after silently dropping invalid items. Preserve the declared denominator and failure reasons.
Inferring a bad optimizer from a loss discontinuity before checking tokenizer, data and sampler identity.
Profiling every run and calling the result normal throughput. Keep diagnostic traces separate and measure observer overhead.

selfTest.q: Saved answers are unchanged but the score changes. Where should you look first?
selfTest.a: Scorer, parser, reference answers, item joins and denominator versions. A training explanation cannot account for an unchanged response artifact by itself.

selfTest.q: What distinguishes a quiet model from a hung process?
selfTest.a: Progress evidence such as completed batches, emitted tokens or committed artifacts, with a declared timeout. A live process alone does not establish useful progress.

selfTest.q: Why keep raw outputs when aggregate metrics already exist?
selfTest.a: They permit item-level diagnosis, independent rescoring and denominator checks without conflating generation changes with evaluator changes.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's joined event ledger, seeded data/resume and scorer-drift incidents, root-cause regressions and observer-overhead measurement.
units.stopWhen: A reviewer can locate each seeded incident's first invalid handoff from stored records, and a targeted regression prevents recurrence without hiding failed attempts.

fit.note: The laboratory names cross-component failures, loader source exposes a real validation boundary, and the watchdog guide adds progress diagnosis. The mini-project supplies joined measurement practice.

units.title: Retry and artifact-commit semantics, cost accounting and governance gates
outcomes: Explain how retry identity, attempt identity and committed artifact identity differ.
Account for failed training, rollout, evaluation, storage and researcher effort without changing sample denominators.
Apply privacy, access, safety and rollback gates to the complete artifact chain.
units.why: A retry can duplicate data or publish half a result. A technically reproducible artifact can still be unsafe or unlicensed to share. These are lifecycle decisions, not end-of-report footnotes.

next.note: Keep the implementation change inside these retry and release boundaries.

study.title: OLMo-core: publication boundaries
study.locator: `Checkpointer.save`, `_prepare_dir`, `_get_tmp_dir`, `_teardown_tmp_dir`, `_temporary_wd` and `_save_metadata`
study.depth: Trace the synchronous local path and contrast the remote-upload branch. Do not infer crash durability or object-store atomicity from the local directory rename. Leave asynchronous execution for Distributed Training.

study.title: Laboratory: failed work and rollback
study.locator: Architecture constraints, Milestone D and Measurement requirements: failed/filtered rollouts, root-cause regressions and rollback criteria

study.title: Compute, safeguards and asset rights
study.locator: Q8 and Q11 to Q13: compute including failed experiments, safeguards, licenses and asset documentation (page read 2026-10-16)
study.depth: Use these as an audit checklist. Skip submission and anonymity procedures. Bring forward the safety release record from the earlier section.

focus: A logical rollout request may have several execution attempts but at most one accepted result under your deduplication rule. Preserve every attempt's work and reason even when only one result contributes to the metric.

Publish immutable payloads, verify completeness and digests, then expose a commit record that readers require. A process dying after payload write but before commit must not make a partial artifact eligible for use.

Count training, generation, verification, evaluation, checkpoint copies and failed retries separately. Keep researcher hours separate from device time; a cheaper device path may require more debugging effort.

Bind access restrictions, license, synthetic-data provenance and the earlier safety gate to artifact identities. Rollback selects the last acceptable artifact and records affected descendants; it does not erase the incident.
units.reproduce: On paper, replay one logical rollout with a timeout, a retry and a late original response. Give each attempt a distinct identity, select one result by a declared rule and charge both attempts. Then interrupt artifact publication before and after its commit record. State which versions a reader may use, which remain quarantined and how a later safety failure revokes acceptance without deleting the audit trail.
traps: Calling retry-until-success unbiased evaluation. Excluding persistent failures can change the population being measured.
Equating atomic visibility with durable persistence. The filesystem and storage protocol need their own durability contract.
Assuming a code repository's license also licenses its datasets, model weights and generated sensitive outputs. Audit each asset separately.

selfTest.q: If two attempts answer one request, should both enter the task metric?
selfTest.a: Not under a one-result-per-request contract. Apply the predetermined deduplication rule, but count the work and retain the outcomes of both attempts.

selfTest.q: A payload exists but its required commit record is absent. May evaluation use it?
selfTest.a: No. Under this protocol it is not published. Quarantine or complete recovery verification before making it eligible.

selfTest.q: The aggregate safety score passes but a privacy slice violates the declared gate. What happens?
selfTest.a: Block acceptance or roll back according to the recorded policy, name the owner and preserve the failing evidence with appropriate access controls. The aggregate does not override the slice gate.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: lmlab's retry/late-result ledger, interrupted artifact publication, whole-study cost record and identity-bound release/rollback gates.
units.stopWhen: The replay accepts no duplicate result or uncommitted artifact, accounts for every attempt and blocks an artifact whose privacy, license or safety gate fails.

fit.note: OLMo-core supplies a concrete publication path; the laboratory and checklist cover retry accounting, costs and governance. The mini-project practices their joint contract.

units.title: A bounded, tested change to a real training or post-training implementation
outcomes: Modify one bounded mechanism in a real trainer without rewriting the surrounding pipeline.
Check unchanged behavior against an independent frozen-batch oracle and changed behavior against a failing regression.
Preserve numerical, resume and failure evidence for the modified path.
units.why: The contribution is a tested change in an actual execution path, not another standalone objective demo. Its boundary must be small enough that the experiment can identify what changed.

next.note: Separate the mechanism from extra tuning, data or evaluation work.

study.title: nanoGPT: a CPU-sized real-code fallback
study.locator: Configuration overrides, `get_batch`, `estimate_loss`, resume branch, checkpoint dictionary and training loop
study.depth: Use this deprecated but pinned implementation if Open Instruct is too heavy. Read `model.py` at the same revision for `GPT.forward` and optimizer construction. Run tiny CPU fixtures with PyTorch 2.14.1 and NumPy 2.5.4; keep compilation, hosted logging and uploads disabled. Stock checkpoints omit RNG and scaler state and are not atomically published.

study.title: Open Instruct: inspect what existing tests actually assert
study.locator: `TestMaskLabels`: `test_has_both_masked_and_kept_tokens` and `test_boundary_masking`
study.depth: Read these assertions beside `mask_labels`. They check presence of masked/kept tokens and selected prefix boundaries, not every label or an optimizer update. Do not download their default tokenizer merely to copy the test pattern.

study.title: Laboratory: correctness before extension
study.locator: Correctness requirements, Milestone D and Milestone F

focus: Choose one seam in the traced implementation: sampler isolation, mask validation, loss reduction or artifact acceptance. State the intended invariant and the smallest counterexample before editing.

A concrete nanoGPT option is separating training and evaluation sampling RNGs. Its stock `get_batch` uses the global torch RNG for both; changing evaluation frequency can change subsequent training batches even without an update.
Use an independent oracle for labels, loss or state, not a second call to the patched helper. Compare logits, loss, gradients and an update on the same frozen batch with declared tolerances.

Reuse earlier resume and regression work. Save any newly introduced RNG or sampler state, reject incompatible old state explicitly, and keep the baseline revision available. Do not bundle unrelated performance changes into the patch.
units.reproduce: In the pinned nanoGPT sampling path, reset the CPU torch seed to 1337 and compare two successive training batches with the same run containing one validation draw between them. Use distinct synthetic train/validation token arrays, batch size 2 and context 16; record the changed training positions. Introduce separate seeded training and evaluation generators and require training positions to stay unchanged by that validation draw. Then round-trip both generator states and test the next draws. This is sampler-isolation evidence, not evidence of improved language quality.
traps: Calling a smoke test an independent oracle. Merely executing the new branch does not check its semantics.
Saving a new generator's seed but not its current state. A seed restarts its stream rather than continuing it.
Assuming the stock nanoGPT iteration cap counts updates as its name suggests. Inspect the post-update termination check and record actual completed updates in your comparison.

selfTest.q: Why can evaluation change training even when it performs no backward pass?
selfTest.a: It can consume a shared RNG stream or mutate mode, buffers or other state. In this sampling example the validation draw advances the RNG used for later training positions.

selfTest.q: What should the RNG-isolation patch preserve on an identical frozen batch?
selfTest.a: The model's forward, objective, gradients and optimizer update within the declared numerical contract. The patch changes sampling ownership, not the objective.

selfTest.q: The new regression passes before the patch too. What is missing?
selfTest.a: It has not demonstrated sensitivity to the defect. Construct a counterexample or inject the old behavior and require the test to fail.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: one lmlab patch to Open Instruct, OLMo-core or the nanoGPT fallback, with frozen-batch, numerical, resume, regression and interrupted-state tests.
units.stopWhen: The regression fails on the baseline and passes on the patch, unchanged frozen-batch behavior matches its oracle, and resumed execution preserves the new state contract.

fit.note: The pool explicitly permits nanoGPT when larger stacks fail local time and setup fit. Pinned source, inspected test assertions and the mini-project provide a bounded real-code route without adding material.
